card.intuition: The same input can produce different output because the model samples from a probability distribution over next tokens — and since one differently-sampled token changes every token after it, a single word difference can become a completely different approach. Provider-side batching and tiny floating-point differences add more spread, and there is no setting that makes it stop.
card.analogy: A roulette wheel that feeds a long chain reaction: the same starting state can end in very different places, and there is no switch for the wheel's tendency to bounce.
card.time_complexity: Retrying is a legitimate strategy on hard tasks — each attempt is one draw from the distribution, so cost is attempts times request tokens, and verification must be re-run against every draw.
card.space_complexity: The input is identical context; what varies is which sampled tokens enter the context on the next request, so the divergence lives on the output side of the token budget.
when_to_use: Retrying a failed attempt, which is one draw that may simply land better
Running automated checks that catch the bad draws, since one passing test can't be trusted to repeat
Staying calm through a string of bad runs instead of narrativizing a model downgrade
gotchas: There's no setting you can flip to make non-determinism go away
A bad week is usually the distribution, not proof that 'the model got worse'

steps.label: Score
steps.annotation: The model produces a distribution over next tokens.

steps.label: Sample
steps.annotation: One token is sampled, often with deliberate randomness to avoid repetition.

steps.label: Diverge
steps.annotation: One different token changes every later token, so approaches diverge.

steps.label: Retry
steps.annotation: A fresh attempt may land within the bell curve of acceptable quality.

exercise.prompt: Simulate sampling without a random module: pick the token whose probability is closest to a given draw value, so the same list can yield different picks.
exercise.starter_code:
def pick(scored_tokens, draw):
    return min(scored_tokens, key=lambda tp: ___________)[0]
hints: Distance from the draw decides which token wins
